SCHOOL COMMUNITY · THE PEOPLE

Who works at my school?

Many people help your school run every day.

Some of them stand at the front of a room, and plenty of others you meet in the hallway, at the gate, in the garden or at the lunch counter — and every one of them is there so your school day works. Walk through all sixteen together and name the ones your child already knows.

People who teach

The faces at the front of the room — and one very important student.

TeacherShows you new things every day — and helps when something feels hard.Art TeacherKeeps the paint, the brushes and the messy, wonderful ideas.Music TeacherBrings the songs, the instruments and the loud, happy endings.Science TeacherSets up the experiments and answers the “but why?” questions.PE TeacherRuns the games where your body gets to run, jump and balance.StudentThat is you — the learner the whole school is here for.
People who help

The helpers your child meets between the bells — at the lunch counter, the library, the office and out in the garden.

School NurseFixes the scraped knee, checks your temperature and sits with you until you feel better.Meet the nurse at the doctor ↗LibrarianKeeps the picture books and knows just which one to hand you next.Cafeteria WorkerServes the lunch — and knows exactly who likes the apple.JanitorKeeps the floors clean, the doors working and the whole school shining.School GardenerWaters the plants and shows you how a seed becomes a snack.
People who keep us safe

The watchers at the doors, the road and the playground — the reason the day feels safe enough to learn in.

PrincipalThe friendly boss of the school — and the office door is open.Visit the Principal’s Office ↗Security GuardWatches the doors and the gate so everyone inside stays safe.Crossing GuardHolds up the STOP sign so you cross the road safely.Bus DriverDrives the bus that brings you to school and takes you home again.Playground SupervisorWatches the playground so the games stay fun and fair for everyone.

Want to print a person? Every card above has a download button right under it — open the whole School People set.

TRY IT TODAY

Which person helps you when you feel sick?

Point at the school nurse card together, then name two more helpers your child has really met — and what they said or did. Naming the people of the school is how a building starts to feel like my school.

Every school is a little different — your child’s school may have more helpers to name. Ask who works at their school and add them to the game.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 16 cards in Who Works at My School, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Who Works at My School. We have 16 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. 02
    Card 1 · Teacher

    “Teacher! This is my teacher. She shows me new things and helps me try. Look how she points at the board — that is where the new stuff lives!”

    How: Play teacher at home: your child at a chair-and-paper "board", you and three stuffed animals as the class. Practice raising a hand, listening for the claps, lining up at the door. The child in the teacher’s shoes stops worrying about the real ones.

  3. 03
    Card 2 · Art Teacher

    “Art teacher! Paint, brushes, glue — and look, an easel! The art teacher says every picture is a good picture. Mine has a purple mountain!”

    How: Make a two-minute gallery: hang three of your child’s drawings with painter’s tape, walk them like a museum and clap for each one. "The artist" loves an audience.

  4. 04
    Card 3 · Music Teacher

    “Music teacher! A guitar! We sing loud, we sing quiet, we clap — boom boom! The music teacher knows a song about EVERYTHING.”

    How: Start an echo song at dinner: you sing two words, your child echoes them, then swap leader. Real music class runs on exactly this game — the leader-and-echo habit transfers on day one.

  5. 05
    Card 4 · Science Teacher

    “Science teacher! A flask — careful, clever! We look, we guess, we try it. Why does the magnet stick? Let’s find out!”

    How: Do one kitchen experiment: sink or float. Fill a bowl with water, gather five small things, guess first, then drop them in. Guessing-then-testing IS science — the science teacher would absolutely approve.

  6. 06
    Card 5 · PE Teacher

    “PE teacher! Whistle — tweet! We run, we jump, we balance. Gym day is the loudest, fastest day of school!”

    How: Animal races down the hallway: hop like a bunny, waddle like a duck, stomp like an elephant, freeze at the whistle (any word works). Real PE runs on listen-then-move — this practices exactly that.

  7. 07
    Card 6 · Student

    “A student! That is ME! I sit at my desk, I listen, I try, I learn. The school is full of helpers — and they are all there for me.”

    How: Play "first day of school" with the card: backpack on, walk to the door, wave goodbye, big hello when you come back. Practicing the day-in, day-out rhythm makes the real one feel known.

  8. 08
    Card 7 · School Nurse

    “School nurse! If I feel yucky or scrape my knee, the nurse helps me. A cool bandage, a drink of water, a sit-down — and soon I am playing again.”

    How: Bandage the teddy: one bandage, one worried teddy, one gentle nurse (your child). Practicing "check it, clean it, bandage it, all better" makes a real trip to the nurse feel like a known story.

  9. 09
    Card 8 · Librarian

    “Librarian! So many books — up high and down low! The librarian finds the best one: about diggers? About bears? Here you go!”

    How: Play librarian at your own shelf: five books face-out, your child behind the "desk" and every stuffed animal asking for a book by name. Pretend checkouts build real library manners.

  10. 10
    Card 9 · Cafeteria Worker

    “Cafeteria worker! Lunch is ready — tray, spoon, apple! ‘Apple or banana?‘ — I choose, and I say thank you!”

    How: Cafeteria night at home: your child takes orders behind the counter and serves the family (real or pretend trays). Serving food is power-role play — picky eaters often taste more when they are the chef.

  11. 11
    Card 10 · Janitor

    “Janitor! Squeak, squeak — the mop! He fixes the door, cleans the spill, keeps our school shiny. What a job!”

    How: Be the cleanup crew: one song, ten minutes, everything back in its basket — then admire the room the way the janitor would. Clean-up feels like a job people do, not a punishment, when it has a name.

  12. 12
    Card 11 · School Gardener

    “School gardener! Watering can — sprinkle, sprinkle! Seeds drink water, sunshine does the rest, and one day — a tomato! A carrot! A bean!”

    How: Adopt one plant — a bean in a cup on the windowsill works. Your child waters it, checks it, maybe measures it with a crayon. Watching a seed wake up is the longest, best yes in childhood.

  13. 13
    Card 12 · Principal

    “The principal! The friendly boss of the whole school. If something is wonderful — or something is wrong — the principal’s door is open. Come in!”

    How: Wave-at-the-principal week: at every pickup, one friendly wave or hello by name. A principal who is a known, smiling person stops being The Scary Office forever.

  14. 14
    Card 13 · Security Guard

    “Security guard! He watches the gate and the doors — careful and kind. Only the right people come in. That is how we all stay safe!”

    How: Gatekeeper game: one child (or a teddy) is the guard at a doorway with a list of who may pass — "bears, yes; dinosaurs, hmm, show me your ticket!" Being the gatekeeper builds understanding instead of fear.

  15. 15
    Card 14 · Crossing Guard

    “Crossing guard! STOP — the sign goes up! Cars wait, feet cross, safe on the other side. Wave thank you — every single day!”

    How: Red light, green light, crossing-guard edition: your child holds a paper STOP sign and decides when the teddy bears may cross the "road" (a rug works). Holding the sign makes the rule make sense.

  16. 16
    Card 15 · Bus Driver

    “Bus driver! Beep, beep! He knows every stop, every name, every bump in the road. On the bus we sit down, we hold on, we ride home!”

    How: Bus pretend: line up kitchen chairs, assign stops (Teddy Street, Dolly Corner) and take turns driving and riding. Practice the two bus rules that matter most: bottoms on seats, wait for the driver’s nod before standing.

  17. 17
    Card 16 · Playground Supervisor

    “Playground supervisor! Whistle — tweet! The games are fair, the line for the slide is moving, and everyone gets a turn. Play on!”

    How: Playground-spotting: at any park, ask your child to find the watching grown-up first (every playground has one). Naming the watcher — at school or at the park — is the safety habit itself.

  18. 18
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  19. 19
    Check

    “Can you find Teacher? Now show me Cafeteria Worker.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  20. 20
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 16 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
